## I notice problems, ask questions, and look for a useful way forward.

I’m **Malik Kolade**, an Economics graduate from **Lagos State University**, based in Lagos, Nigeria. My other name is Ishola. My interests span data analytics, quantitative research, and building tools that help people get things done.

What connects these interests is the way I think. When I encounter a slow process, a confusing task, or something people struggle to access, I want to understand what makes it difficult. I ask questions, break the problem into smaller parts, and look for a solution that fits the people who will use it. Sometimes that means analysing data. Sometimes it means organising information, improving a workflow, or building a reusable tool.

## Building around the people who need the solution

My reusable portfolio website grew out of a problem among friends and colleagues: they wanted a place to present their skills and work online, but they could not code or were uncomfortable with even basic programming. Their need was clear; the technical steps stood in the way.

I approached that as a practical problem to solve. Rather than expecting everyone to learn web development before sharing their work, I developed a reusable portfolio structure with pages, project layouts, and an editing guide. The aim was to reduce the work involved in getting started and give people a clearer route to maintaining their own portfolio.

That experience reflects what matters to me when I build something: understand the difficulty, make the solution usable, and explain how someone can continue using it. A tool becomes more useful when its user can understand what to do next.

[Read the portfolio framework story](projects/reusable-portfolio.qmd){.project-link}

## Bringing that approach to business and research

At **ALFA STORE**, I maintained sales records and saw how repetitive calculations slowed everyday work. I developed a digital costing and reconciliation tool, with an approximately **80% reduction in calculation time** reported in my CV. That experience connected accurate records with a practical operational improvement.

In my **Bank Marketing analysis**, I focused on a decision: how a bank might prioritise limited campaign capacity. I compared models, examined the trade-offs between precision and recall, and used customer ranking to make the results easier to interpret in a business context.

My Economics background gives me another way to approach questions: consider the incentives, constraints, and wider conditions behind the numbers. I graduated with a **4.35/5.00 CGPA** and contributed to literature reviews, research design, analysis, and interpretation across **25 undergraduate research projects** during my university experience.

## How I work

::: {.card-grid}
::: {.info-card}
### Understand the difficulty
Start with the person, process, or decision. Ask what is getting in the way and what a useful outcome would look like.
:::
::: {.info-card}
### Build and check
Break the task down, test assumptions, and check whether the analysis or tool answers the original need.
:::
::: {.info-card}
### Make it understandable
Explain the result, document the workflow, and be clear about limitations and what still needs improvement.
:::
:::

## Teaching has shaped how I communicate

Through tutoring and academic mentorship at **Afkindemy**, I support students with admission preparation, academic planning, and coursework. I have also taught a class of 25 pupils and represented more than 170 students in university academic and welfare discussions.

These experiences have made clear communication part of how I work. People come with different levels of knowledge and confidence; a useful explanation should give them a starting point and help them take the next step.

## What I’m developing next

I’m strengthening my skills in **Python, Pandas, NumPy, SQL/MySQL, Excel, Stata, EViews, and R**, alongside applied data science training at **TS Academy**. My direction is to combine sound analysis with reproducible workflows and practical tools for business and research.

I’m interested in opportunities where I can investigate a question carefully, learn what I need, and contribute a solution that people can use.
